description: ERECTION OF A FIRST FLOOR SIDE/REAR EXTENSION AND REAR DORMER ROOF EXTENSION TO FACILITATE THE CREATION OF 1 SELF-CONTAINED DWELLING TO THE SIDE OF EXISTING DWELLING AND ASSOCIATED X2 PARKING SPACES AND CYCLE AND REFUSE STORE IN FRONT GARDEN
subdivision_of_building: The land to the side of 143 Lower Morden Lane
decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed landscaping and extensions would fail to achieve a high standard of design, by reason of design, siting, bulk and massing which would result in a poor quality, dominant, overly bulky form of development which, coupled with earlier extensions, would integrate poorly with and be harmful to the appearance of the subject dwelling and the visual amenities of a prominent corner site, and would detract from a sense of openness at the junction of Lower Morden Lane and Cardinal Avenue. The proposal is therefore contrary to London Plan (2021) policies D3 and D12.3 and D12.4 of Merton's Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 2 - The proposed development would result in a cramped and poor standard of accommodation to the detriment of the amenities of future occupiers due to inadequate internal and external space standards. The dwelling would fail to provide an acceptable standard of residential accommodation and living space resulting in a cramped and unsatisfactory standard of accommodation to the detriment of the amenities of future occupiers. The proposals would therefore be contrary to policy D6 of the London Plan 2021, Merton Local Plan 2024 policy D12.3 and DCLG Technical Housing Standards -nationally described space standard 2015.

Reason : 3 - By reason of the absence of a Demolition/Construction Logistic Plan (including a Construction Management plan in accordance with TfL guidance), the scheme fails to demonstrate it would not adversely the free flow of traffic and pedestrian and vehicular safety on the surrounding roads. The scheme fails to comply with, in particular, Policy T6 of the London Plan and Policy T16.1 and T16.3 of Merton's Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 4 - By reasons of absence of completed Merton's Energy Assessment Template for Minor Residential Schemes detailing how the development will meet Merton's minimum requirements, absence of plan drawings identifying the proposed location of low carbon heat and renewable energy generation technologies, lack of plans showing any retained, refurbished and new build element and proposed use of gas fired systems with absence of information to justify why low or zero carbon systems cannot be used, the proposal fails to comply with Merton Local Plan 2024 policies CC2.1, CC2.2 and CC2.4.

Reason : 5 - By reason of absence of a completed Good Homes Alliance Overheating Risk Tool, Dynamic overheating modelling outputs or other supporting information demonstrating how the risk of overheating has been mitigated the proposal fails to comply with Merton Local Plan 2024 policies CC2.1, D12.2 and D12.3.

Reason : 6 - By reason of absence of As Designed internal water calculations and specifications for any proposed water fittings to demonstrate the development will achieve internal water usage of less than 105 litres per person per day, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the application would meet the requirement of Merton Local Plan 2024 policy CC2.6.

Reason : 7 - The application has failed to demonstrate that the proposed development would secure a net biodiversity gain and in the absence of a S106 to secure the self build exemption for the Biodiversity Net Gain the proposal fails to comply with Environment Act 2022, policy G6 of the London Plan 2021 and Merton Local Plan 2024 O15.3.

Reason : 8 - In the absence of a fire safety strategy, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the development would provide the highest standard of fire safety, thereby failing to comply with policy D12 of the London Plan 2021.

Reason : 9 - In the absence of a site specific flood risk assessment and sustainable urban drainage system commensurate to the nature and scale of the development the scheme is considered to increase risk of flooding in the locality contrary to the aims and objections of, in particular, London Plan policy SI 13, Merton Local Plan 2024 policy F15.7, F15.8 and F15.9.

Reason : 10 - INFORMATIVE
Note to Applicant
In accordance with paragraph 38 of the NPPF, The London Borough of Merton  (LBM) takes a positive and proactive approach to development proposals focused on solutions. LBM works with applicants/agents in a positive and proactive manner by:
"	Offering a pre-application advice and duty desk service. 
"	Where possible, suggesting solutions to secure a successful outcome.
"	As appropriate, updating applicants/agents of any issues that may arise in the processing of their application.
In this instance:
"	The application was not considered to comply with the provisions of the Development Plan and NPPF as submitted, and would have required substantial changes such that a new application would be required. 
"	The applicant is advised to seek pre-application advice on any resubmission.
